html:
Griqualand West was a British colony in central South Africa around the diamond fields of Kimberley, from 1871 to 1880, when the Cape Colony absorbed it. The map still shows it as a separate territory in 1880 and 1900.

The land belonged to the Griqua, an Afrikaans-speaking people of mixed Khoikhoi and European descent who had set up small states beyond the Cape frontier, and to Tswana communities. Then diamonds were found, and in 1871 the Kimberley diamond rush began. The Griqua chief Nicolaas Waterboer, the Orange Free State and the Transvaal all claimed the fields. Britain backed Waterboer's claim and then annexed the land itself.

Kimberley became the richest place in southern Africa. There Cecil Rhodes bought up the claims and in 1888 formed De Beers, which controlled almost all of the world's diamond supply.
